latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer n>1, a real number x, and an integer m. We show that E_n(x+m)=E_n(x).

By the basic property of the floor function, if z is an integer then floor(t+z)=floor(t)+z for every real t. Since km is an integer for each integer k, we have
floor(k(x+m)) = floor(kx+km) = floor(kx)+km
for every k=1,2,...,n.
In particular,
floor(n(x+m)) = floor(nx+nm) = floor(nx)+nm.

Therefore
E_n(x+m)
= floor(n(x+m)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+m))/k
= (floor(nx)+nm) - sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)+km)/k.
Now simplify the sum:
sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)+km)/k = sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + sum_{k=1}^n m = sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nm,
because (km)/k = m for each k.
Substituting this into the previous line gives
E_n(x+m) = floor(nx)+nm - (sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nm)
= floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
= E_n(x).

Hence E_n(x+m)=E_n(x) for all integers n>1, all real x, and all integers m.
